subject: PulseMD: prompt collection & eval plan
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@pulsemd.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: PulseMD: prompt collection & eval plan

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on evaluation and data handling:

Summary from call:
- PulseMD wants an automated triage assistant for inbound patient messages and scheduling clarifications (short clinical summaries, triage urgency flags).
- Primary concerns: accuracy for clinical intent, hallucination risk on medication details, and PHI redaction before sending to third-party evaluators.

Proposed evaluation approach:
1) Prompt set collection — you provide ~200 representative prompts covering triage, scheduling, and edge clinical queries (we'll accept CSV or JSONL).
2) Redaction pass — provide guidance on PII/PHI to remove prior to sharing with our eval team. We can accept a redacted and an original version, but redwood will only store redacted versions on hosted evals unless you opt into a private workflow.
3) Benchmarks — we will run a quality/regression suite using our standard clinical prompt benchmarks plus a PulseMD-specific holdout set; results will be shared in the Drive link below.

Immediate asks for PulseMD: 
- Please upload an initial sample file with 40–60 prompts that reflect real volume and edge cases (free-text examples are best). CSV template attached (pulsemd_sample_prompts.csv).
- A short attachment or bullet list describing what must be redacted (names, MRN, SSN, specific PHI patterns). If you prefer, fill out the attached PDF with examples.

Operational notes: we can run the first evaluation on our hosted infra within 48–72 hours after we receive samples. If you prefer a private eval (to keep data in your VPC), we can schedule that — will require a short security review.

Next steps (proposed):
- You upload sample prompts + redaction guidance by Tue, Nov 17.
- Redwood runs initial model-fit checks and shares a scoreboard + recommended model variants by Nov 19.

Ben (cc) will be the technical lead for ingestion and redaction questions. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you'd rather walk through the sample format.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: pulsemd_sample_prompts.csv (template)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@pulsemd.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: PulseMD Clinical Team <clinical@pulse-md.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PulseMD: prompt collection & eval plan

Thanks, Evelyn — great outline. We're aligned on the approach. I attached an initial batch of 55 prompts (pulsemd_sample_prompts.csv) and a short PDF with redaction rules (pulsemd_edgecases_and_redaction_notes.pdf). Highlights:

- The sample set includes: 30 triage messages, 15 scheduling/confusion cases, 10 edge clinical queries (medication contradictions, prior-authorization mentions).
- Redaction rules: remove full patient names, MRNs, and email addresses. Replace DOB with age in years when relevant. For medication mentions keep drug name but remove dosage when present.

A couple of notes we want you to pay attention to during eval:
- We see false-positive urgency flags when patients use terms like "severe" colloquially; model needs context sensitivity.
- Safety: avoid making definitive clinical recommendations (we prefer conditional phrasing).

Attachments included: pulsemd_sample_prompts.csv, pulsemd_edgecases_and_redaction_notes.pdf

Let us know if the CSV layout works; we can export more from our message queue. Also looping in our Clinical Ops lead if needed.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Head of Clinical Products, PulseMD
sarah.liu@pulse-md.com

Thanks for the samples, Sarah — quick technical clarifications from the eval side:

1) CSV schema: the template expects columns [prompt_id, raw_text, category, patient_age, is_sensitive(example boolean)]. If you exported differently, please confirm column names or we can normalize on ingestion.
2) Edge cases: could you flag 6–8 of the most troublesome examples in the CSV (add a column "edge_flag"), especially the ones that previously tripped your rule-based routing? That will help prioritize failure modes in the first run.
3) Redaction resilience: would you be comfortable sharing two versions of 10 edge prompts — original and redacted — so we can validate that our redaction heuristics do not remove clinically relevant context? If you prefer not to share originals, we can run a synthetic extraction test.

Operational question: if we find a quality regression between model variants during the bracketed eval, do you have an internal reviewer who can make quick accept/reject judgments (15–30 min) on flagged outputs? That will speed up model selection.

I'll put together an ingestion window for next week; Evelyn, can you confirm preferred SLA for turnaround?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Evaluation Programs
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Sarah — appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed redaction doc. To confirm next steps and timing:

- We've ingested the CSV and verified schema for the 55-row sample. Marissa's team will normalize any column mismatches and flag 8 edge cases as requested; we will add an "edge_flag" column in the normalized file and share back by EOD Nov 23.
- Redwood will run the initial model-fit checks across three candidate families (2 open variants + 1 quantized variant) and post results to the eval page: https://redwood.app/evals/DEAL-PMD-2026-11 by Nov 24. The attached benchmark PDF shows metrics we will surface (intent accuracy, hallucination rate, urgency precision/recall).
- If we observe regression on clinical fidelity, our recommended mitigation will be: conservative prompt templates, adjust temperature/top_p, and apply a post-generation validator for medication mentions. We'll document suggestions in the scorecard.
- We can do a 30-minute review with your clinical SME for any flagged outputs; please let us know who can join short-notice reviews.

Deliverables and dates:
- Nov 23: normalized CSV + edge_flag column (Redwood)
- Nov 24: initial scoreboard + recommended model variant + short write-up
- Nov 30: optional private-eval kickoff if PulseMD requests VPC-only processing (needs security sign-off)

Permissions note: We will only surface redacted text in the shared eval dashboards. If you want us to include originals in private VPC-mode, we will follow the security checklist and an additional ADR.

Thanks — looping Ben for ingestion scheduling.
